scope: Observed routine candidates; not a complete function inventory or disassembly

candidates.hypothesis: ULA output pulse/delay segment, likely used for the Spectrum beeper
evidence: Menu snapshot PC and bounded execution trace visit the range repeatedly.
Private local static inspection shows repeated ULA port output changes separated by countdown loops; no instruction listing is stored here.
During short menu keypress trials the tested CPU was in this segment rather than a keyboard read.
unknowns: Actual enclosing function entry and callers
Whether this invocation represents music, an effect, or another timed signal
Cycle accuracy and later menu input timing

candidates.hypothesis: Cluster of screen drawing routines, potentially masked or XOR-composited game objects
evidence: An isolated 200000-step gameplay CPU trace recorded all 1141 screen writes at twelve instruction-start addresses between 0xBA59 and 0xBB4C.
Repeated calls to 0xBA0D and 0xBA8C were observed in the same trace.
The cluster read 174 distinct addresses in page 0xD000 and 191 in page 0xF000 during this diagnostic run; their data layout is not yet known.
Private local static inspection of those reachable paths supports read/modify/write operations into display memory; no assembly is stored here.
unknowns: Exact routine boundaries and whether the calls draw sprites, background, or both
Per-object mask and attribute data layouts
Behavior with original frame interrupts and input timing
